title: World's largest banks, by total assets
source_name: The world's largest banks by assets, 2026
definition: Total assets as reported (as-reported basis, not adjusted for differing accounting standards such as US GAAP vs IFRS), ranked among the world's 100 largest commercial banks, as of Dec. 31, 2025, adjusted on a best-efforts basis for pending/completed M&A
notes: Rank and country columns included in staging file for reference; only bank name and total assets (US$bn) are merged. Full 100-bank table extracted from Wikipedia's 'List of largest banks' article (fetched via MediaWiki API, not hand-transcribed), which reproduces the S&P Global Market Intelligence ranking; verified against S&P Global's own published article text, which confirms rank-1 Industrial and Commercial Bank of China at $7.646 trillion (matches staged value of 7645.80) and a Dec. 31, 2025 data date.

title: Forest area
source_name: FAOSTAT Land Use domain (RL), Forest land / Area
publisher: FAO (Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations)
definition: Total forest land area: land spanning more than 0.5 hectares with trees higher than 5 meters and a canopy cover of more than 10 percent (or trees able to reach these thresholds in situ), excluding land predominantly under agricultural or urban use. FAO FRA definition.
notes: Bulk CSV: https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/Inputs_LandUse_E_All_Data.zip (Inputs_LandUse_E_All_Data.csv, Item=Forest land, Element=Area, unit 1000 ha, converted to sq km at 1000 ha = 10 sq km). 'China, mainland' row used for China (excludes Hong Kong SAR, Macao SAR, Taiwan, which have no FAOSTAT forest-land row of their own). Dependencies/territories that FAOSTAT reports as their own distinct rows alongside a separate parent-country row (Guadeloupe/Martinique/French Guiana/Reunion/Mayotte vs France; Faroe Islands/Greenland vs Denmark; Bonaire-Sint Eustatius-Saba/Aruba/Curacao/Sint Maarten vs Netherlands; Hong Kong/Macao vs China; UK/US overseas territories) are left as-is, not summed into the parent -- each parent's figure is FAOSTAT's own unmodified national row. Nicaragua's most recent FAOSTAT value is 2022 (flagged L/missing for 2023-2025); included as the country's latest available figure. [vintage override: date=2025, expected 2024-2025; 1 row(s) older than 2024]

title: Total Nobel Prize wins
source_name: Nobel Prize API v2.1, laureates endpoint
definition: Total number of Nobel Prizes (all six categories: Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature, Peace, Economic Sciences) awarded to individual laureates, tallied by country of birth (modern-day country, i.e. historical birthplaces mapped to today's borders). Excludes prizes awarded to organizations, which have no country of birth.
notes: Faroe Islands and Guadeloupe births merged into Denmark and France respectively (constituent parts of those states); Scotland and Northern Ireland births merged into United Kingdom. 3 of 990 individual laureates (Abdulrazak Gurnah 2021 Literature, James A. Robinson 2024 Economics, John M. Martinis 2025 Physics) have no birthplace recorded in the Nobel API and are excluded, so totals may undercount by 1 prize each for their (unknown) birth countries.
